## Live verification of the DEFERRED criterion — preconditions MET, one step awaiting approval

Session picked this up expecting to implement. It is already implemented and LANDED: the wiring
merged to `origin/main` as **`ab885cef6986`** ("fix(infra): wire Jira credentials to on-box MCP"),
carrying `rebar-ticket: 5ec7-d681-9616-43ed`. The earlier unpushed worktree commit `0f1d0cfc7792`
is that same change; `ssm.tf` and `fetch-secrets.sh` are byte-identical between the two. No code
change was needed this session.

### Both blockers named in the previous comment are now CLEARED

- **`user_data.sh` templatefile breakage is fixed on main.** Lines 91-92 now read
  `$${!PARAMS[@]} / $${PARAMS[$name]}` — both halves escaped. Tracked separately as
  `rubied-nonvagrant-whimbrel`.
- **`terraform apply` HAS RUN and succeeded for these parameters.** All four are now in the remote
  state (`terraform state list`, read-only, S3 backend):

      aws_ssm_parameter.jira_project
      aws_ssm_parameter.rebar_plain_seeded["/rebar/prod/jira-url"]
      aws_ssm_parameter.rebar_plain_seeded["/rebar/prod/jira-user"]
      aws_ssm_parameter.rebar_secrets["/rebar/prod/jira-api-token"]

  So the three import blocks adopted the operator-seeded parameters, and `/rebar/prod/jira-project`
  was CREATED by terraform (String, Version 1, 2026-08-27T16:44:16 us-east-1) — it did not exist at
  the time of the previous comment. This ticket is therefore **no longer blocked** behind
  `improvised-altophobic-azurevase`; that ticket's `mcp-client-pat-*` parameters are still absent
  from state and still block other terraform work, but not this.

### SSM holds real values, not the `CHANGEME` placeholder

Established WITHOUT displaying any value, by comparing SHA-256 digests against the digest of the
literal string `CHANGEME` (`ba01338ba5fa`):

    /rebar/prod/jira-url         String        v2   len=30    is_CHANGEME=no
    /rebar/prod/jira-user        String        v2   len=22    is_CHANGEME=no
    /rebar/prod/jira-project     String        v1   len=3     is_CHANGEME=no
    /rebar/prod/jira-api-token   SecureString  v2   len=192   is_CHANGEME=no

`jira-project`'s digest equals the digest of `REB`, matching `rebar.toml` `[jira] project = "REB"`.
The v2 on the three adopted leaves is the expected post-import PutParameter (SSM bumps the version
on any `Overwrite=true` write, including a same-value one); `ignore_changes = [value]` held, as the
non-placeholder digests prove.

### The four variables REACH the deployed container, exactly once each

Live container `rebar-mcp-25ea12c200ae-8092` (image `compose-mcp:25ea12c200ae...`, healthy),
`docker inspect .Config.Env`, names and lengths only:

    JIRA_URL       present=yes len=30
    JIRA_USER      present=yes len=22
    JIRA_PROJECT   present=yes len=3
    JIRA_API_TOKEN present=yes len=192
    total JIRA_ lines in the container env: 4

Every length matches its SSM parameter exactly, which is what makes this non-vacuous: the values in
the container are the values in SSM, so `fetch-secrets.sh` demonstrably read them and materialized
them into the compose `.env`. **Exactly four lines, one per variable** — none is duplicated, so the
`.env`-only carriage held and this change did not reproduce the double-definition defect filed as
`calcite-farsighted-goose`.

### The credential CODE PATH executes in the deployed environment

Ran inside that container, against rebar's own resolver — the exact function the description named
as the fail-closed point:

    access_check._resolve_probe_scope(None)
      jira_url:       present=yes len=30
      jira_user:      present=yes len=22
      jira_api_token: present=yes len=192
      jira_project:   present=yes len=3
      -> scope RESOLVED (returned creds, NOT the INVALID verdict)
      -> jira_project = REB

Neither `missing_credentials` nor `missing_project` is reached. That is the specific regression the
fourth variable was added to prevent, now falsified in the deployed environment rather than inferred.

### Liveness anchors — positive AND negative control

Read-only authenticated calls from inside the container. Nothing was created or modified.

    POSITIVE  GET /rest/api/3/myself        -> HTTP 200, accountId present, active=true
    POSITIVE  GET /rest/api/3/project/REB   -> HTTP 200, key=REB, id present
    NEGATIVE  GET /rest/api/3/myself with the last 4 chars of the token corrupted -> HTTP 401

The negative control is the part that makes the positives mean anything: the probe can see failure,
so "HTTP 200" is evidence of a working credential rather than of a check that never ran. No token,
credential or accountId value was printed — the accountId was reported as a truncated digest.

### Codebase criteria re-verified on current `origin/main` (565e1856bc9d)

    pytest tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py \
           tests/interfaces/facades/test_bridge_programmatic.py
    96 passed in 128.75s

That covers the SSM leaf types + import adoption, the `jira-project` == `rebar.toml` drift guard,
the `.env` emission and its decryption posture, the compose/`mcp_run_new` parity via
`_ENV_FILE_ONLY`, and the soft-degrade posture.

### STILL OUTSTANDING: the `bridge_check_access` verdict itself

Not run, deliberately. `access_check.run_access_check` is a MUTATING probe against production Jira:
it creates an issue in REB, adds a label, writes an issue property, JQL-searches it, then deletes
it. If it fails between create and delete it leaves a real probe issue in REB, which the reconciler
could later treat as inbound work. That is a shared-system change, so it is an operator decision,
not this session's. Awaiting approval; the read-only evidence above already establishes that the
credentials, the project scope and the code path are correct in the deployed environment.
